subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps by repairing pi-tui redraw behavior, adding OpenClaw-owned viewport/follow anchoring, or exposing an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: Source evidence shows a credible renderer and TUI update path, but the best repair changes terminal UX policy and may require dependency ownership or a new user-facing setting.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then only follows new output when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add TUI auto-scroll preference
options.body: Expose a terminal setting if maintainers want explicit user control, accepting the added settings surface and fresh/upgrade validation burden.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture proves the exact jump and redraw reason.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then only follows new output when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has repeated TUI and pi-tui integration history, making him the best available owner for the dependency-versus-local-policy choice.
